title: Conditional kappa = 0.001301970637653655: geometric intersections and rational paired whole-owner hosting
body:
This adds `research/tensor-nonroot-pairs`, an offline source-bound finite construction with conditional kappa = **0.001301970637653655**, approximately **0.3456% above PR473 at 4bea72f5cfa700dba4556bdb5d2761d7577b7a6c**. It uses an explicit GL cover and the inherited compiler/analytic contracts; it is not an unconditional integer-multiplication theorem or a Lean certificate.

## New mechanism

The old kernel search intersected sets of named E8 roots. We instead intersect their actual rational spans. This exposes 56 auxiliary directions of the form e_i +/- e_j that were invisible to that representation. The selected construction adds 22 response-kernel pivots on top of the updated rank139 basis and response retiming. Their simultaneous source-bound word changes the local paid histogram by +84 rank1 and -53 rank2; all 955 arbitrary-dirty columns and 22 omission controls pass.

These new entrance lines need non-coordinate residual routes. Two copies have an explicit rational orthogonal 16-by-16 normalization: their intact rank7 residual projectors are orthogonal and sum to a rank14 coordinate projector. We place each pair inside ONE owner family, with two restored spectator directions. No logical residual is split across different physical families. Full 78-column owner maps include the actual port/window basis, the entrance directions, placement and inverse; matching dimensions alone is not accepted.

The physical program contains 88 complete local invocations, 62,920 whole residual occurrences,968 paired blocks and 1,733,496 emitted events, including 23,040 bridge updates. All costs are recomputed from this one program; gains from different proposals are never added numerically.

## Exact price and scope

- Final kappa: 1301970637653655 / 10^18.
- Bit saving: see the exact rational bracket in EXPECTED.json; approximately 0.001303667975.
- Unchanged complex saving: 1305231506267591 / 10^18.
- Live stock 9600, physical stock 9609, rank mass 745536, deficit 3264.
- Physical prefix 1684 bits, charged 1728.
- Concrete route 224 elementary factors per direction, conservatively charged 512.
- PR490 GL-cover sharp bad-class charge and enlarged row allowance 28416 are used. The fixed-q weighted-routing constant B_GL stays explicit in the symbolic bootstrap cutoff.

This does not claim to beat PR480's higher cross-copy headline. That claim retains the disputed operator admission discussed in PR448/451; no such split is used here. The construction also does not achieve the larger campaign target.

## Reproduction and validation

    python -B research/tensor-nonroot-pairs/verify.py /absolute/new/output

Python3.11+, SymPy, C++17 and Boost are required. Set CXX/BOOST_INCLUDE if necessary. No network, annealer or discovery optimizer is required. Default rebuilds both suppliers. `--complex-output` accepts only the exact completed complex receipt and 87 implementation/17 output hashes pinned in the package; any reuse is explicitly reported.

Checks include source reconstruction, fresh native legality and five-/eleven-stage columns, 1,019 positive Gram frames, exact auxiliary-line decoder,22 omitted-correction controls, rational route/inverse/projector/factor controls, actual full-matrix owner injection, complete chronological emission, independently reconstructed physical-family row invoice, two rational moment engines, six bootstrap rounds and 47 strict inequalities with next-grid/degenerate-parameter controls. VALIDATION.json and release receipts specify the packaged run; finite verification does not discharge the inherited all-size contracts.

Two representation fixes are explicit and source-bound: the decoder's full-frame mask uses 176 lines while retaining 120 semantic ports, and half-inner-products remain rational instead of being floored. The general integer-basis native auditor is unchanged.

## Direct credits

- **PR473**: updated rank139 basis exchanges, exact nested response source and whole-owner packing framework.
- **PR483**, **PR478**, **PR476**: response cancellation, nested flags and target-factor lineage retained in the base word.
- **PR485**: the scoped coordinate-kernel analysis motivated searching actual geometric intersections rather than named roots.
- **PR490**: fixed-GL whole-owner transport, sharp fallback, row28416 and explicit routing cutoff.
- **PR470**, **PR472**, **PR463**, **PR443**: R715 word, retiming, shared-response construction and checked local interfaces.
- **PR471**, **PR458**: unchanged complex supplier, full-nine-axis normalization, paid wrappers and same-owner spectator handling.
- **PR442**, **PR451**, **PR465**: hosting/compressed-stage infrastructure and fallback-accounting lineage.

The immutable-source retiming is reused from our earlier unpublished tensor-syndrome-portfolio package and adapted to the new basis; we do not claim to have invented it again. Classical rational linear algebra, two-square/Hadamard normalization and quaternion four-square identities underlie the new routing. Existing license and source notices are retained.

## Saved research for future work

The package includes the general four-copy rational hosting proof, exact two-copy witnesses, the auxiliary-intersection method, independent composition review, and the tested complex partial-response/centre-lattice routes with their paid-cost limitations. PR484's larger complex-supplier proposal was studied but is not silently included in this exponent. Overlapping candidate counts, optimistic profiles and uncompleted routes are explicitly separated from the achieved construction. Nothing was published by the assistant.

title: Under review (split-residual interface): cross-copy idle-axis hosting, one residual on two copies of one idle child; computed κ = 0.001330733966732373 not established
body:
Conditional **κ = 1330733966732373/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.330733966732373·10⁻³**, bit-bound, **+5.13 % over #447** (1.265848755025709·10⁻³, complex-bound), +7.53 % over #442 and +17.44 % over #434. Neither local word changes: complex #433 (R = 560, m = 73), bit #434 (R = 747, m = 64). The idle windows are #442's.

## Change

In #442's idle-axis hosting a whole helper residual sits inside the pending coordinates of one data family. Bit residuals have width 8 − e (637 of width 8, 104 of width 7, 6 of width 4) and complex residuals width 9, while the idle children have ranks 7/14/28/42 (bit) and 8/16/32/48 (complex). A rank-7 child cannot hold a width-8 residual, a rank-14 child holds one and wastes six coordinates, and so on: 6,944 of the 45,360 pending bit coordinates per replica and 5,760 of 51,840 complex ones stay idle and are paid as remainder children.

A child acts on every copy (side, port) of its pair, and all copies share the child's window. This package lets a residual lie across the pending sets of **two copies of the same idle child**. With P = P₁ + P₂ the identity D_{P₁}·D_{P₂} = D_P (the parents' D_{P'}·D_{P−P'} = D_P) writes the dirty invocation's factor on the residual as a product of a factor on each family; each is moved to the child exactly as in #442 §2, since the window is a property of the pair; and each child's remainder is exact by #442's fact (b). Every child's capacity, copies × rank, is then a multiple of the residual width, so the remainders almost vanish. A residual never spans two children or two pairs. The route is still an elementary coordinate permutation of the address space; the finite invoice charges one further route factor per helper selector.

The selection is an integer programme over counts n(child, stage, width) on the concatenated tape of each child's copies (maximise Σ ln(m/r) × hosted coordinates, subject to availability and, on the bit side, exact width-64 tiling of the leftover). `SELECTION.json` freezes it; `--discover` recomputes it with scipy.

## Result

| supplier | #442 saving | this saving | live stock | hosted residuals (split) | max child |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bit, m = 64, R = 747 | 1.239085·10⁻³ | **1.332507·10⁻³** | 9,457 → 8,592 | 46,160 of 53,784 (12,496) | 24 |
| complex, m = 73, R = 560 | 1.267453·10⁻³ | **1.437532·10⁻³** | 8,400 → 7,680 | 40,320 of 40,320 (13,720) | 48 |

Both rank deficits stay 2496. The bit max child 24 is one partial copy of a rank-28 child; the complex max child 48 is the 133 copies per replica of the rank-48 final children that the complex supply cannot fill (5,040 residuals against 5,760 width-9 slots per replica). Since #447 is complex-bound at 1.267453·10⁻³, the complex component here should also lift #445/#447's eleven-stage bit words; that composition is not claimed.

`python3 -B research/cross-copy-hosting/verify.py /absolute/new/output` (Python 3.11+, standard library only; the output directory must not exist). It

2. regenerates both hosted templates from #434's fresh outputs and the frozen selection;

5. runs #434's strict outer assembly: six bootstrap levels and all 47 inequalities, with the next grid point and the zero-η, zero-β and unit-β controls rejected.

body:
## A stronger complex supplier: b = 1326789535340266/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.326790·10⁻³ (+4.68% over #442), whole-residual hosting, one owner per family

This adds one self-contained package, `research/e8-complex-gauge-kernel/`. It is a **complex-side supplier**: #433's split-centre word (R = 560, m = 73), #442's idle-axis hosting with the one-helper-per-family rule of #458, and two tools of the bit side ported to it. **No new κ is claimed in this package.** With #442's bit word the bit side binds (κ = 1.237552·10⁻³; 1.279171·10⁻³ with our pinned R724 word). #493 reports κ ≈ 1.325·10⁻³ when its R489 bit word is paired with this supplier; there the complex side binds. #496 and #497 re-place this word's helpers and report 1.332077·10⁻³ and 1.325118·10⁻³. The current lemma-less κ frontier is #478 (Dugongue) at 1.295509·10⁻³, which sits at #458's complex cap; this supplier raises that cap; #458, #460 and #462 are bit-bound, not complex-bound. On the complex side b is +2.28% over #458 (1.297204·10⁻³) and +1.65% over #471 (1.305232·10⁻³; #471 admits our kernel79 through normalisation plus same-owner spectator borrowing, and is credited below). This raises the complex cap of this lineage to κ ≤ 1.325031·10⁻³ (the #448/#450 lineage used in #464 and #469 has complex roots of about 1.44·10⁻³). It is conditional on two lemmas, the review points: **Lemma A** (paid residual wrappers with explicit spectators; the entrances are isotropic, not coordinate entrances) and **Lemma G** (nonzero-frame compensation and the centre scatter). It supersedes the draft #449.

| complex word | entering helpers | entrance rank | b (·10⁻³) | gain over #442 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| #442 | 0 | 0 | 1.267453 | |
| shared-donor kernel | 79 | 79 | 1.305684 | +3.02% |
| entrance gauges | 80 | 106 | 1.306413 | +3.07% |
| **both** | 122 | 148 | **1.326790** | **+4.68%** |

### Relation to #458 and #471
#458 (chafreaky) puts the 79-pivot kernel of #449 on an eleven-stage complex word and pays its entrance transforms as emitted, checked adapters, with at most one helper per host family per invocation. This package adopts that treatment on the nine-stage word and adds the entrance gauges; #449's hosting allowed several helpers on one family and left an entering helper's spectator coordinates unplaced, which #458 showed is not sufficient. #471 normalises the complete invocation and borrows spectators in the same owner array; this package applies the same borrowing to its banks (an entering helper is the only owner of its bank family in an invocation, its spectators are the first cells of the bank's pad) and extends the one-owner rule to every register class of an invocation, with a control for each.

### Change
A helper's frame-zero compensation (the response of its arbitrary dirt) pins it to start frame {0}, so its residual has width 9. Two exact ways avoid it:
- **Shared-donor kernel** (#417/#435/#434/#439/#440): a pivot whose response column is a rational combination of donors' columns starts at an entrance E contained in every member's first frame; each donor receives `d += −q·pivot` at E before the main word (inverse after cleanup).
- **Entrance gauge** (#401/#408–#416): the compensation of a helper is executed at its entrance frame E instead of frame 0; targets climb through the nested entrance chain, and each centre copy descends from its frame through the levels it serves (mass-neutral, rank deficit 2,496).

A helper that starts at E has the residual S_E = T_FULL·T_E⁻¹ = L_E (C_[w] ⊗ I) R_E, w = 9 − dim E, exactly (global phase included). The paid wrappers R_E⁻¹ before the whole invocation and L_E⁻¹ after its cleanup turn it into the coordinate factor and restore the e = 9 − w spectator coordinates; they are emitted, replayed, decoded and charged. Widths 8/16/32/48 of #442's idle children are tiled by width-8 residuals; the hosting is whole-residual with distinct stages in every copy and at most one helper per physical family per invocation, with the host chart (residual vectors, first unused basis vectors as spectators) in the route and audited. Residuals that are not hosted go to banks of their own, one entering helper per replica per bank family, with the spectators in the pad and the route and chart audited in the same way.

### Result
Both rational moment engines certify b = 1326789535340266/10¹⁸ (next grid point rejected). Under the one-owner rule the word hosts 39,792 of 40,320 residuals whole; the other 528 (all of width 8) sit in 66 banks (live stock 7,746, maximum child 9, rank deficit 2,496). The finite invoices with the hosted stock and the wrapper charge, and the strict outer assembly (six bootstrap levels, 47 inequalities, next-grid, zero-η, zero-β and unit-β controls rejected), pass for #442's bit word (run here, κ = 1.237552·10⁻³ unchanged) and, as a pinned input from our own bit-side package that is not re-run here, for the eleven-stage R724 mixed word under whole-residual hosting (c = 1.280810·10⁻³): κ = 1.279171·10⁻³, bit-bound (no new κ). That pairing is informational; our R715 word is #463.

### Checks (`python -B research/e8-complex-gauge-kernel/verify.py DIR [--all] [--discover-check]`)
- #442 runs unchanged (with #434 and #433 below it), then the **regression anchor**: with the empty selection the generalised scripts reproduce #433's canonical word, local programs, local checks, parent global template and independent replay, and #442's hosted template and `HOSTED.json`.
- Gauge + kernel word: exact arbitrary-dirt and inverse-transpose replay (800 columns); emitted program replay in both orientations with centre lifetimes and wrappers; independent read-back of the serialized stream; exact Gaussian recipes with global phase for every used frame transition (`complex_phases_full.py`, unmodified); exact decoding of the wrapper monomials (L⁻¹ S_E R⁻¹ = C_[w] ⊗ I on every entrance frame); independent hosting audit (windows, slots, owners, spectator chart on data and bank families, one owner per family on every register class, private namespace, remainders, wrong-width control); fresh finite invoices; certified b.
- **Independent Lemma G stage** (`code/lemmaG/`, imports no package script): the label / scalar / accounting checker on both orientations, the exact operator identities of every compensation, centre and helper instance on all 512 basis columns, the complete emitted program end to end against the transform computed from definitions, and 14 necessity mutants of the clauses.
- Mutation controls, all rejected, several through the certifying scripts themselves: kernel and gauge gates, entrances, target levels, centre chains, wrappers, centre descent steps, two helpers on one data or bank family (accepted by #442's rule, rejected here), spectator records, owners in the private namespace or on another replica's families, wrappers on non-helper registers, and selection-level conditions; the generators also refuse the eight-entering-helpers-per-bank tiling.
- `--discover-check` recomputes the frozen hosting selections with HiGHS and requires equality. Status: the full `--all` runs pass from fresh copies on Python 3.14 (`--all --discover-check`), 3.12 (`--all`) and 3.11 (`--all --discover-check`), with identical summaries. The `.gz` inputs of the Lemma G stage are pinned by the sha256 of their decompressed JSON, since gzip container bytes depend on the zlib of the Python in use.

### Principal review points (conditional)
- **Lemma A** (`PROOF.md` §3). Exact and checked: S_E = L_E (C_[w] ⊗ I) R_E and the wrapped product on every entrance frame. Assumed: #458's argument that wrappers around a whole invocation of a family on which nothing else acts leave the spectators identical, at nine stages, for hosted families and banks.
- **The entrances are not coordinate entrances.** Every entrance frame consists of even-weight vectors of F2⁹ (15 of 16 frames totally isotropic). The bit-style criterion of #440 (`validate_isometries`) is not met and cannot be met by any orthogonal map of O(9,2); restricted to entrances that meet it, the gain is 0. #442's complex audit asserted `w == 9` and #433's emit start frame 0 for compensated registers; the marked copies here generalise exactly these.
- **Lemma G** (`PROOF.md` §2): reduces to #425's conjugation lemma and #471's / #458's virtual entrance, plus a schedule lemma (hypotheses (a)-(d)) whose clauses are checked on the emitted streams by the independent stage above; new relative to #458 and #471, which do not use the gauge.
- All interfaces inherited from #370, #386, #425, #433 and #442 remain assumptions. This is a conditional finite witness, not a theorem.

### Credits
Dugongue (#471), chafreaky (#458, #417, #439), DaysSky (#442), icekylinx (#433), jacklightChen / Zhihao Chen (#386, #425), rohanarun (#434, #435, #438), eumemic (#436, #437, #440, #441), #471 (normalisation of the complete invocation, same-owner spectator borrowing), the authors of #401 and #408–#416 (entrance gauges and prefixes), Dylan Crow (#370), Jacob Sussman (E8 unit); #451 for the cross-family obstruction.

title: Replace local Gaussian inverse branches with two convolutions
body:
The retained phase-cell inverse uses a difference of two convolution pairs. This package replaces its online interior operation with a classical q-Gaussian factorization: two triangular convolutions and three diagonal factors inside the existing similarity. The new proof explicitly bounds the difference from the independently rounded, width-truncated source. The global H, exact Schur setup, sparse couplings and periodic boundary system remain unchanged; the complete error still fits the original scalar interface.

The weighted triangular factors also have norm below 3p, and tensoring the central formula produces five stages without branch expansion. **No new κ is claimed.** A fast joint weighted evaluator, its routing/padding and tensor boundary composition remain unproved. The existing dimension-dependent cost and small-field exposure still bind.

An exact guard also rejects prematurely rounding the unweighted tensor kernel to the scalar P-grid before reweighting. It checks all 4,096 entries of a small three-axis operator and a uniform admissible parameter family where a significant weighted entry disappears. The latter uses symbolic exponent inequalities, not enormous tensor executions. This does not rule out implicit kernels, adaptive precision or other FFT implementations.

Validation: fresh full wrappers on macOS Python 3.11/3.14 and Linux aarch64 Python 3.12 passed with byte-identical complete CHECKS and RESULT files. Checks cover 1,950 LDL identities, 1,950 inverse entries, 2,084 rounded local entries with actual signed integer packing and up to 115 reciprocal guard bits, 3,024 complete original-Schur output entries using the new local operation plus the retained rounded boundary/coupling maps, 756 tensor identity entries, 1,856 weighted-factor entries and five rejected mutants. These finite checks support the conditional written proof; they are not a complete multiplication theorem. GitHub CI is separate.

Reproduce: `python3 -B research/branchfree-gaussian-inverse/verify.py /absolute/new/output` (Python 3.11+, standard library only). Package manifests, ten Git-checked source pins and fresh receipts are included.

Attribution: the q-calculus identity is classical (Kuznetsov, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1507.02959, with the specialization derived in PROOF.md). title: Conditional kappa = 0.001297375468897877: response retiming and stage-conditioned donor flags (+0.05929% over #483)
body:
This adds `research/tensor-syndrome-portfolio/`, a standalone source-bound construction and offline replay package.

**Conditional kappa = 0.001297375468897877**, exactly `1297375468897877/1000000000000000000`: **+0.059291495% over #483** (`0.001296606691405309`). The bit supplier binds. This is a whole-family result; it does not claim to exceed #480's `0.001372550159367980`, which uses the distinct disputed cross-copy admission.

## Mechanism

1. **Response-preserving injection relocation.** Search the cosets of the transported target-response map, retaining only immutable-source rewrites. Move source5's injection into helper452 earlier to frame480; reconstruct the literal inverse cleanup. Equal nonzero responses preserve the target on every input, including dirty helpers. The actual witness simplifies to commuting additions into one receiver. In each invocation ranks1 and3 are replaced by rank4, strictly improving the recurrence moment for every exponent in(0,1). Deletion-only and insertion-only controls both fail.
2. **Stage-conditioned nested donor inventory.** Choose the one-upgrade provider at stages2,4,6,8 in every replica and the eleven-upgrade provider elsewhere. Their residual-width inventories fit different idle windows differently. Each of88 complete calls names its provider, exact word/program hashes, entrance frames and explicit isometry map. Every one of62,920 residual occurrences remains whole on one family; no cross-family split or independence shortcut enters the construction.

The crossover combines coding/control response kernels with compiler register allocation. Response-preserving retiming and heterogeneous dispatch are not claimed as newly invented mathematics: earlier gate retiming and our R740 portfolio already existed. The new concrete construction is their stage-conditioned application to R715 nested donor flags, with the new source-injection witness. The price is computed from the complete emitted mixed program, never by adding gains.

title: Batch Gaussian boundary right-hand sides to reduce their cost
body:
The retained Gaussian phase-cell inverse applies one banded boundary matrix to many independent tensor lines. This groups a power-of-two number of right-hand sides and uses exact Strassen products for blocked triangular solves, Woodbury correction and sparse cell couplings. The conditional boundary factor drops from `w^2` to `w^(log_2(7)-1)`.

The proof pays for RHS grouping, single-field padding, table scans, ragged blocks, cyclic endpoints and returns. A residual bound independent of the number of cells retains O(p) precision. The exact inequality `7^16 < 2^45` gives the conservative boundary margin `(3+29r)/32-delta`, replacing `r-delta`.

**No new kappa is claimed.** Per-axis Gaussian work, small-field exposure, `epsilon+r<1`, normalizations and supplier/assembly contracts remain. This follows #475 and #479 in removing a separate outer cost; changing only this row leaves the current selected minimum unchanged.

Checks cover 15 signed/near-singular/degenerate cyclic systems, two actual Gaussian-derived Schur systems, 2,781 inverse entries, 2,952 complete Schur comparisons, exact Strassen operation counts, 54 split/interleave layouts and six non-vacuous mutations. body:

title: Bind the selected gen4 certificate to fresh replay outputs
body:
`gen4-bank-verify` checks the selected record against its frozen certificate and runs a fresh supplier replay, but does not compare that replay's certificate with the frozen publication. This adds the missing comparison after a successful replay and makes the dedicated workflow use the same Make target.

The helper compares the complete current certificate recursively, preserving JSON types, field sets and array order while accepting equivalent exact rational strings. It binds the frozen bytes to the selected digest, the fresh positive kappa to the selected values, and the receipt to the source manifest, file count and all nine stages. Only the receipt's nonnegative finite timings may vary. Make stops on temporary-directory, supplier or binding failure; workflow path filters cover the relevant inputs and tests.

Validation of this exact four-file patch:

- Independent bounded review: 1,894 cases passed (1,747 expected rejections and 147 acceptances), including separate changes to every one of the 177 certificate leaves in fresh and frozen outputs, and five Make scenarios using command stubs.
- All 14 authored tests passed independently and again in a clean worktree on Python 3.14.8: `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_selected_replay.py' -v`.
- The patch applies cleanly to main at `12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b`; reconstructed files match the independently reviewed bytes.

**Still unverified:** the full source-bound supplier replay, actual `make gen4-bank-verify`, Python 3.11/3.13 CI and global `make verify`. The historical joint-dual manifest already pins a different Makefile hash on the base; this separate compatibility issue is not repaired here. The Python matrix, dependency/action pins, regeneration step and clean-tree check are retained.

This checks consistency after a trusted replay. It does not authenticate a standalone receipt, establish execution by itself or prove the shared certificate's mathematics. No certificate, selected value, source manifest or theorem changes. A bounded check of current PR descriptions and related Make/checker variants found no duplicate of this selected-gen4 binding; no exclusivity claim is made.

title: Formalize the indexed B_K scalar bridge and bind the pinned B3 word
body:
This adds a standalone Lean formalization of the existing normalized scalar borrowing chain, including descending cleanup and the signed endpoint. Stage-indexed composition is proved for every nonempty finite list of bank pairs over any abelian group. The nineteen-operation B3 term is definitionally equal (`rfl`) to the three-pair indexed chain.

Each stage must satisfy its explicit complete normalized shear and helper-preservation contracts for every input. Under those contracts, signed exchange restores every bank and the shared helper state, with arbitrary correlations allowed. Physical frames, owners, endpoint operators, scratch lifetimes, costs, all-size compilation and analytic transfer remain separate obligations.

The included `bridged.py` snapshot is pinned to Git blob `626a28614b07066528fd5f189d87cffa5015ac60`. Replay uses hash-locked selected-AST recognition outside the Lean kernel, compares the generated term byte-for-byte with the submitted target, and never executes upstream Python. It requires an already installed Lean 4.33.0 and performs no downloads.

Validation: fresh temporary builds of all three modules at trust level zero; 22 transitive axiom reports with no `sorryAx` or project-defined axioms; five rejected controls covering twin sign, cleanup order, unsigned endpoint, stage index and helper threading. The new correspondence results use no axioms; other new results use `propext`, with `Quot.sound` additionally used by the generic correlated endpoint.

This formalizes the existing Jacob Sussman/PR363/373/375 bridge lineage, also inherited by PR377/381/390. It claims no new borrowing mechanism, correlated-helper insight, global novelty or priority, and does not certify PR390's heterogeneous physical provider. Source attribution and license text are included.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001350580884553120: gate-frame retiming of #450's eleven-stage cross-copy word (+0.2105%)
body:
Conditional **κ = 0.001350580884553120**, `8441130528457 / 6250000000000000`, above PR 450 (`35094327`) by `567267367657 / (2 * 10^17)`, which is **0.2105 percent**.

## Summary
- Retimes PR 450's target-mixed R740 word. 113 phase-B deliveries move to coarser frames of the pinned family. Every ordered scalar addition is unchanged, phase A is unchanged, and phase B is re-listed by frame dimension.
- The retiming is a frozen witness, applied by `code/retime_apply.py` with input and output content hashes pinned. 18 changes are applied to PR 443's word before PR 450's target mixing, and 95 after it.
- The local profile per call moves from `{1:2460, 2:1012, 3:276, 4:315, 5:108, 6:42, 7:14, 8:9}` to `{1:2401, 2:1019, 3:291, 4:315, 5:99, 6:60, 7:5, 8:9}`. The local cost per call falls from 25,612.68 to 25,555.04. The bit root rises from `674781707224226878971 / (5 * 10^23)` to `1352407420162920171433 / 10^24`. The assembly stays bit-bound with 6.29 percent of complex slack.
- Entrance frames and residuals are untouched, so the frozen hosting selection, the global template, live 1200, 8140 hosted residuals, maximum child 56, halving depth 3 and row allowance 28416 are PR 450's. The complex side is PR 448's.
- `verify.py` runs PR 450's verify.py unchanged first and requires its published kappa. It then runs PR 443's legality, formal-column, mutation and Gram checks and PR 450's mix check with its four controls on the retimed word, followed by PR 450's eleven-stage global template, hosted audit with 20 mutations and assembly.
- Three negative controls on the witness format are rejected: wrong input word, a delivery moved to a frame of the wrong dimension, and donor deliveries moved across their mix frame.
- Every improving move is in phase B. Phase-A gates sit at their minimal support frames. Further gains need gate-structure changes, outside this format.
- This branch includes PR 450's commits and its fix for the two evidence files that `.gitignore` had dropped.

## Test plan
- [ ] `python3 -B research/e8-eleven-stage-retimed/verify.py /absolute/new/output --quick` prints `PASS_ELEVEN_STAGE_RETIMED_COMPOSITION` and the kappa above
- [ ] `<output>/parent450/RECEIPT.json` carries PR 450's kappa

Credits.

The race word and its engines are @DreamingOfClouds's (PR 450), with the five-stage packages and the exact-interval moment and outer-assembly engines. The R740 word and its checkers are @chafreaky's (PR 443, PR 445). The cross-copy hosting is @higherbeing's (PR 448), and the idle-axis hosting is @DaysSky's (PR 442).

The single and paired gate retimings of @eumemic (PR 437, PR 440, PR 441) are the special cases this search generalises. The sharp bit charge is @Srikrishnabalaji's (PR 461), and the three-stage cover note that proves it is @icekylinx's. The compressed geometry is @jacklightChen's.

- @Bortlesboat (Andrew Barnes): aligned pair groups (PR 2).

- @dleen (David Leen): retained totals and stage sharing (PR 4).
- @jacklightChen (Zhihao Chen): ternary five-subset network (PR 7), translated frames (PR 21), semantic precision and bulk resampling (PR 23), two-stage controlled corners (PR 29), deferred endpoints and signed phase correction (PR 97).
- @icekylinx: batched recursive networks (PR 10), partial-swap networks (PR 18), endpoint gauges (PR 24), structured projector blocks and bulk assembly (PR 32), copied centers (PR 36), stopped product-ring interchange (PR 104), partial source gauges (PR 115), three-stage Cayley covers (PR 130).

title: Finite assembly, source-basis cost reduction, and E8 verification
body:
This PR contributes constructive finite assembly parameters, a reusable reduction in the bit supplier’s finite overcharge, a parent-contract guard for the hosted bit audit, and faster source-equivalent hashing and scalar replay in the E8 emitter. Earlier bank optimization and verification tools are retained.

Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave an avoidable gap below the balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive theorem and exact verifier that select finite parameters for **every rational target below `min(b,c)/(1+min(b,c))`**, given admitted bit and complex caps and the retained conditional interfaces.

The [new package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier) chooses strictly positive backoffs, a finite number of bootstrap steps and explicit integer cutoffs. The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md) establishes termination and all 47 retained strict outer inequalities. It also proves maximality on a supplied rational grid, relative to these caps and this assembly family. The ceiling itself is not attained.

### Reusable source-basis finite-cost reduction

The [source-basis package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order) now provides a guarded postprocessor that derives the copied forms from the actual input word. It preserves their order, their literal inverse, the set of source rows entering the full frame, and the surrounding construction. A separate postprocessing stage lets it compose with frozen reset/kernel selections without changing their original hashes or receipts.

| Pinned construction | Complete finite coefficient | Two-level coefficient | Extra local additions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR433 R758 | 223 to 192 bits | 483 to 420 bits | 32 |
| PR438 R747 after resets/kernel | 226 to 193 bits | 488 to 423 bits | 32 |

The added operations are fully charged. The lower cancellation-free prefix dominates that added cost. **Both supplier caps and the multiplication exponent stay unchanged.** This improves a rigorous finite overcharge; it makes no practical runtime or current numerical lead claim. It is not guaranteed to improve every word.

The PR433 five-stage changed-bit run is retained. On [PR438](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/438), pinned at `e3b56de7869f6af88d48ac0ab1d7959c4c9e6176`, all nine stages passed in one 18.49-second run: original construction/reset/kernel checks, the separate basis stage, and unchanged exporter/global/audit/price/combined checks. The new word restores all 987 local and 7,683 global columns, with eight bank controls, four outer controls and all 47 strict inequalities passing. Its κ remains `45340333148791/40000000000000000`.

The candidate has a fresh complete invoice. The baseline cost is reconstructed from its literally replayed word and the unchanged verified geometry/schedule; its full global pipeline was not rerun. Eleven unchanged outputs from the independently completed PR433 complex component are explicitly reused, with source, canonical-word and recipe bindings. No new complex or phase execution is claimed.

The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order/PROOF.md), source bindings, exact executed adapters, original/new words, receipts and stage logs are retained. The self-contained audit independently checks both constructions' literal orientations, copied forms, omission controls, prefix growth and complete invoices. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 75-input package; manifest is `3df3113896b1130f2770f26da08ec7f4b812e822d568cce69b0f75ba7eb2cd17`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/verify.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/test_postprocess.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/postprocess.py original.json candidate.json
```

Three focused test contracts cover both exact reconstructions, input preservation and idempotence, unsafe basis interfaces, and CLI overwrite protection. The output is a candidate: each new word still needs its supplier's complete admission checks. The postprocessor and offline audit are portable. The retained PR438 adapter records the exact executed temporary paths; it is evidence, not a portable CLI. The existing PR433 full replay wrapper has input-only validation, with its original completed scientific run retained separately.

### Preserve the inherited contract in the hosted bit audit

The original [PR442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/442) generator preserves its parent scalar schedule, but its independent bit hosting audit does not enforce that preservation. On the authentic published hosted template, deleting the terminal exchange or zeroing a bridge coefficient is accepted with an unchanged paid profile, although literal F2 replay finds eight or three wrong scalar columns, respectively. **These are deliberately mutated regressions; the actual published construction is not alleged invalid.**

The new [guard and integration patch](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-hosted-bit-contract) enforce the parent schedule, scalar columns, levels, invocation headers and inherited template fields. Only the bit generator's documented hosting changes are permitted. The original ownership/profile audit remains required; the complex side has different permitted edits and is outside this guard's scope.

The positive fixture exactly matches PR442 commit `4e16d001d505d4f21dd2bcfc44591f9be4c279bd` and template payload `dd7833dcaff8c84b258847f4c4d65b6402c702700ae37d2c464083ee37b24126`. One seven-stage, 4.43-second bit-only reconstruction reused an exact completed reset word, then ran the original kernel, exporter, source-span check, global emitter, parent audit, hosted generator and regression probe. The parent kernel's three controls and audit's eight controls passed. No complex, phase, pricing or assembly replay was performed; no new bound is claimed.

Four focused test contracts cover the authentic positive, the two original-audit false negatives with independent scalar replay, sign/level/header/index/field mutations, and a matching invalid parent/child pair. The offline verifier checks the source/Git bindings, payload hashes, logs and receipts, and executes the exact two-line integration patch in memory. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 38-input package, manifest `f15db9c1ae361b6d0b1f230a23cf6da02add4ea70c1e5907c80d42d9301eac57`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-hosted-bit-contract/verify.py
```

### Byte-identical emitter digest caching

The [emitter cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2c47125cbb0619dc63ccdf64c9c583f064240aeb/research/e8-emitter-digest-cache) removes repeated JSON serialization from the pinned [PR447 emitter](https://github.com/rohanarun/integer-mult-bounds/blob/43e5aa3a2fb6701b1facf542f7f3dee0fbb33c3e/research/e8-eleven-hosting-selected/code/emit.py). It encodes each immutable instruction tail once per orientation and each owner descriptor once per call. A minimal integration patch preserves event order, paid-rank increments, ownership assertions and all other emitter checks.

Across **2,742,552 records and 144 calls** from completed PR438 and authentic PR442 bit workloads, every record byte, independent complete digest, event count and local paid profile matches. The exact source-extracted hashing loop measured a median **3.206 seconds before and 0.587 seconds after**, a **5.47x hashing-loop speedup**. Three alternating trials include cache construction. Template loading, geometry checks, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8, not a whole-emitter speedup or a fresh PR447 scientific replay.

The byte-preservation proof covers the pinned event schema and immutable inputs. The portable offline verifier checks source/Git/fixture/receipt bindings, exact patch scope, every record, and two focused contracts for JSON escaping, large integer tails, fresh per-call owners and malformed inputs. The recorded adapter and original notices are retained. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes. Package manifest: `f45b0dd2c710838f4e5df1c1450c444a7235720b286e89ba946612081c5f847f`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-emitter-digest-cache/verify.py
```

Default verification does not rerun the benchmark. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted loop on another machine.

### Stage-local address caching for scalar replay

The [scalar address-cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/e500c9c4217483de882cf06e6e80b25b70ea1ca5/research/e8-scalar-address-cache) removes repeated local-to-global mapper calls from the same pinned PR447 emitter. Its two-line integration patch constructs one address table per local stage, including the private scratch index. All original scalar, dirty-helper, private restoration, stage, terminal and integer bridge controls remain intact.

On two retained local-word workloads, three alternating trials measured **1.736x and 1.730x faster scalar replay**, respectively: **35.984 to 20.728 ms** for the completed PR438 word and **35.774 to 20.676 ms** for the authentic PR442 template's local word. Timing includes address-table construction and the complete extracted scalar-replay section through its 24 bridge-omission controls. Template loading, AST extraction, geometry, hosting, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8; the cache adds O(LOCAL) storage per active stage.

Both versions independently return identical complete values, levels, schedules, stage receipts and controls. The contract checks **648,692 operand mappings**, both reflections, all **11 stages and 9,417 basis columns per workload**, private restoration and all 24 bridge controls. The retained PR438/PR442 local words are used with the pinned eleven-stage recipe; this is not a fresh full PR447 admission. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes, and no whole-emitter speedup is claimed.

The proof states the valid-index and stage-immutability preconditions. The portable offline verifier binds original source/Git/license/fixture/receipt bytes, checks exact patch scope, repeats the complete equivalence contract, and covers address-block boundaries, per-stage cache freshness, invalid operands and omission of the private endpoint. It also reproduces identical combined source when the address and digest patches are applied in either order. Their separately measured speedups must not be multiplied into an overall speedup. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 32-input package, manifest `643da0bb1ae5f1453f0c31574ac78b08ec7c3f9836126a8c4dbdedeef8cf61af`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-scalar-address-cache/verify.py
```

Default validation does not repeat timing or any supplier wrapper. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted section on another machine.

### Finite-assembly worked example

Using the unchanged suppliers from [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned to `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`, the greatest admitted point on a `10^-27` grid is

```
kappa = 280216238064569651155257 / 250000000000000000000000000
      = 0.001120864952258278604621028
```

This is strictly above that source's `0.001120864952258278`, by approximately **6.04621e-19**. The numerical gain is tiny. The reusable parameter theorem and verifier are the main contribution; no new supplier word, practical speedup or global optimality is claimed. Later supplier contributions, including [PR434](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/434), report higher bounds. This pinned example is not a claim to the current numerical lead; the parameter theorem applies to future admitted caps as well.

One clean default replay of the pinned supplier package passed all 13 stages in 6.19 seconds. It regenerated both changed programs, their scalar and ownership checks, moments and finite invoices; the original verifier reused its source-bound Gaussian phase evidence. We did not rerun every Gaussian pair. Actual receipts and all stage logs are retained. The new verifier independently reproduces the original assembly, recomputes both supplier moments and the selected seed with two rational engines, checks the actual 483-bit two-level coefficient against its 512-bit charge, and verifies nine finite bootstrap steps and all 47 strict inequalities. The next grid point, zero eta, zero beta and unit beta are rejected.

Five focused tests cover both binding components, equal caps, 48 cap/target regimes, exact grid endpoints, 100-digit grids, zero-step cases and invalid premises. Ody independently reviewed the proof and code and reran the complete package successfully. All 50 package inputs match manifest `876412045fcd74e87bba4f02704eb312fad77e565e73eecb1c4849e1df92ff8d`. The CLI also exports witnesses whose rational numerators exceed Python’s default decimal conversion limit; an end-to-end 100-digit-grid regression covers this. An integration test connects this offline verifier to the existing Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 test matrix, without a new workflow or executor.

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Add `--output /absolute/path/to/new-result.json` to retain every exact parameter, cutoff and margin. Python 3.11+ and the standard library suffice.

**Current signed head:** `e500c9c4217483de882cf06e6e80b25b70ea1ca5`. The scalar address-cache package passes its default offline contract and focused repository integration test, with independent review by Ody. **All 56 CI jobs passed on this head:** [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38160852534), [terminal elimination, 2 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38160852467), and [recycled registers, 2 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38160852516). The previous signed head `2c47125cbb0619dc63ccdf64c9c583f064240aeb` passed all 56 jobs: [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38149787308), [terminal elimination, 2 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38149787217), and [recycled registers, 2 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38149787178). All package audits and focused regressions use the existing Python matrix; no workflow or executor was added. Scientific-run, measurement and reused-evidence scopes are stated above.

### Earlier contributions retained

- [Exact bank optimizer](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-exact-bank-optimizer): necessary-and-sufficient packing conditions, optimal patterns and minimum replication for the width-73 rank family. An independent exhaustive oracle checks 16,875 inventories.
- [Chart-sensitive dirty-endpoint audit](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-dirty-chart-audit): exact all-address Gaussian checking, including a counterexample invisible at address zero and an admitted positive control. Six focused regressions pass. Its obstruction is scoped to the stated independent-bank interface.
- [E8 retimed component verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-retimed-component-verification): retained emitter, phase, lifetime and finite-accounting evidence for the pinned PR384 complex component.
- [Weighted donor-rank matching](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/gen5b-weighted-matching): the earlier reproducible construction reused by later contributions. Its historical conditional bound is `0.000751075693834608`; later suppliers improve it.

The supplier compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. This is a conditional finite construction, with no unconditional multiplication theorem or new Lean proof.

New parameter selection, source-basis ordering and postprocessor, hosted-bit parent-contract guard, emitter digest and scalar address caching, proofs, tests and evidence integration: George Lydakis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody's independent review. PR447's emitter retains rohanarun's original notices and Codex-assistance attribution. PR442's hosting construction and original audit retain the DaysSky package's original notices and Claude-assistance attribution. PR438's reset/kernel construction remains credited to rohanarun; the kernel method and exact engine retain Chafik Boukhalfa's (chafreaky) attribution. PR433's construction remains credited to icekylinx with OpenAI Codex; its upstream lineage includes Zhihao Chen, ai-nanachi, Dylan Crow, Jacob Sussman and the retained contributors. The unchanged outer engine retains its eumemic/Anthropic Claude, icekylinx, Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures credits. Original notices, licenses, source pins and earlier package attribution are preserved.

title: Conditional κ = 0.001347744547714835: eleven-stage cross-copy hosting with target mixing (+1.278% over #448)
body:
> **Caveat (added after #451).** #451 shows that #448's cross-family residual split is not an exact factorization: D_(a+b)⊕I has trace 90, against 54 for D_a⊕D_b. This package's word splits 1,807 of its 8,140 hosted residuals across two different data families, and #451's trace argument reproduces exactly on our (4,4) splits. **The κ claimed below therefore rests on #448's routing derivation as disputed in #451, and should be treated as not established** until a fully charged compiler or a regrouping theorem covers these splits.
> - Under whole-residual hosting (no split), with the same checks: this word gives κ = 1.265848755·10⁻³, bound by #442's complex supplier (bit c = 1.2730520·10⁻³). Unmixed it gives 1.263365465·10⁻³.
> - The target-mixing lemma and the eleven-stage construction are independent of the dispute.

Conditional **κ = 269548909542967/(2·10¹⁷) = 1.347744547714835·10⁻³**, **1.2783% above #448** (1.330733966732373·10⁻³). The bit supplier binds, at **c = 1.349563·10⁻³** (+1.28% over #448's 1.332507·10⁻³). #448's complex supplier is unchanged (b = 1.437532·10⁻³, nine stages) and has 6.5% of room.

title: Conditional kappa = 0.001274548075945587: full-nine-axis kernel normalization and same-owner spectator borrowing
body:
This adds `research/e8-tensor-normalization/`, a self-contained replay package for the changed construction.

The composed conditional exponent is:

**kappa = 1274548075945587 / 10^18 = 0.001274548075945587**

This is **+0.6303146486% over #456**. The source snapshot is frozen through #457; this comparison makes no claim about later PRs.

## Mechanisms

### 1. Normalize the complete dirty-helper invocation

For each one-dimensional complex entrance E, the exact helper endpoint is:

    Phi = T_full T_E^-1

We factor this as:

    Phi = L (C8 tensor I1) R

Here L and R are explicit Gaussian monomial maps. Wrapping the complete local call with their inverses admits the desired operation while preserving all nine physical dimensions, global phases, and arbitrary dirty contents.

The scalar-backward program retains its original frame chronology and uses the same endpoint wrappers.

### 2. Borrow the inactive ninth axis from the same owner array

The eight active axes lie inside the pending idle child. The spectator lies in its orthogonal complement within the same ambient array.

The complete invocation acts as identity on that borrowed coordinate. Consequently, only the eight active axes are removed from the child's paid remainder. Every simultaneous invocation has a disjoint full physical footprint and an explicit orthogonal route.

This construction does not split a helper across owner families or fit a nine-dimensional function register into eight dimensions.

Together these mechanisms admit **#449's existing 79-pivot response kernel**. The separate gauge-80 modification is not used. The witness applies the complete kernel in all 77 calls of the seven-replica, eleven-stage construction and explicitly records all 6,083 spectator borrows.

## Composition

| Supplier | Construction | Lower saving |
|---|---|---:|
| Bit | #457 rank151 + #450 target mixing + reused #455 two-prefix recovery | 0.001276174621854442560268 |
| Complex | #449 kernel79 + the admission mechanisms above, using #456's seven-replica layout | 0.001305231506267591 |

The bit supplier binds.

The complex moment's finer lower endpoint is 0.001305231506267591990847. Assembly conservatively rounds this downward to 18 decimal places. Gains are composed through the supplier profiles and outer assembly, never added.

The complex profile is:

    {1:153851, 2:71764, 3:4807, 4:17248, 5:33266,
     6:2, 7:2254, 8:6356, 40:1, 64:2046}

Its ambient dimension is 89, live stock is 8,400, physical stock is 8,978, rank mass is 744,744, and deficit is 2,856.

Monomial wrappers are charged per ambient array entry, including every exterior slice. The invoice conservatively charges sixteen real primitives for every helper per complete call and includes the existing routing/compiler reserves. No clean full-array temporary is assumed.

## Reproduction

```sh
python -B research/e8-tensor-normalization/verify.py /fresh/output/directory
```

Requires Python 3.11+, SymPy, a C++17 compiler, and Boost headers. Set `CXX` and `BOOST_INCLUDE` where necessary. Replay requires no network, optimizer, or Lean installation.

Checks include:

- Changed bit native compilation, legality, formal columns, stage composition, Gram frames, and whole-owner routing.
- Both 800-column complex scalar orientations, 2,932 exact phase edges, and 240 data endpoint adapters.
- Fourteen canonical entrance wrappers, each checked on 512 Gaussian-dyadic columns, with 70 negative controls.
- Independent ownership and active/complement replay, full nine-axis orthogonal routes, and complete-program dispatch.
- Rational moments, conservative finite invoices, six bootstrap levels, all 47 strict assembly inequalities, and adjacent-grid and parameter controls.

## Sources and attribution

Direct reuse: **#449, #456, #457, #455, #450, #451, and #454**.

The hosting/compiler/word lineage additionally includes **#442, #433, #425, #417, #386, #377, and #370**. The outer formula follows **#434/#315**.

Exact pinned sources and retained notices are recorded in `PROVENANCE.md` and the manifests. We do not claim the public response kernels, target-mixing identity, whole-pool framework, or reused prefix recoveries as new discoveries.

Earlier tensor-isomorphism work suggested two structural adaptations:

- Paired primal/dual coordinate changes suggested the endpoint normalization.
- Active/complement projectors and orthogonal-block constructions suggested the restored spectator borrowing.

The multiplication identities are established separately in `PROOF.md`; these connections are mathematical inspiration, not imported Lean certification.

## Research record and future directions

`RESEARCH.md` preserves the unsuccessful screens and their scope, including Steinberg/transvection rewrites, terminal-observable substitutions, common-frame centralizers, cleanup compression, and full-footprint-only allocations.

The conservative E510 admission produced only a small gain. Permitting an explicitly restored spectator in the same owner array changed the allocation constraint and admitted all 79 pivots.

A smaller 112-pair ablation establishes strict moment improvement using:

    16^alpha < 2 * 8^alpha, for 0 < alpha < 1.

The next useful target is the binding bit supplier, including a rigorously justified bit analogue of spectator borrowing. Further complex-only saving does not currently improve the composed exponent.

## Scope

The inherited all-size supplier, hosting, compiler, and outer-assembly interfaces remain conditional.

This is not an unconditional sub-n-log-n multiplication theorem or a fresh Lean certificate. It supplies concrete local and storage arguments, finite witnesses tied to pinned sources, and a replay of the changed construction.

+0.741% over #458. Whole-residual hosting on both sides: no cross-family residual split, no cross-copy lemma, no new complex lemma.

| side | supplier | endpoint |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| bit (binds) | **R715** E8 bit word, eleven stages, #442 whole-residual hosting, target mixing | c ≈ 1.285129·10⁻³ (+0.712% over #459's 1.276042·10⁻³, +0.742% over #454's) |

#465 (Srikrishnabalaji) has independently certified this outer assembly (the step #463's draft left open) at 1.283479306671789·10⁻³
with a sharper bit charge, crediting #463; this PR supplies the full bit supplier and its verifier.

**What is new: the bit word R = 715** (#436's R740 → 715).
1. **A carrier lower bound, and a word that meets it.** In this format a copy of source x_s that first acts above its line frame
   serves only targets in a hyperplane section of s^⊥ (frames contain everything they touched). The 63 lines of E7 = s^⊥ are a
   spherical 4-design, Σ_r ⟨r,u⟩²⟨r,v⟩² = 16(|u|²|v|² + 2⟨u,v⟩²) > 0, so no two hyperplanes contain them: every source needs ≥ 3
   registers, i.e. **≥ 240 carriers**; likewise every target needs ≥ 2 helpers reaching its hyperplane (240, met since #370).
   #370-lineage words spend 272 carriers because each frame line 2e_m enters the D4 sums of seven blocks. **Frame-pair D4 sums**
   (D4(c) = Bcw[c] + FP + FP', FP = 2e_a + 2e_b over the 12 pairs of one AG(3,2) direction plane) meet the bound: R 740 → 724.
2. **Eleven cancelling re-expressions** (a rule rewritten as x ⊕ y of existing symbols; overlap cancels inside its frame): R 724 → 715.
3. #443's replica kernel rebuilt for the new word (deterministic search, coordinate entrances), and #450's target mixing
   **generalised to chained receivers** (a donor that is itself a receiver); it reproduces #450's mixed word byte for byte.

**Verification** (`python -B research/e8-r715-paid-complex/verify.py /abs/out`; CI workflow `e8-r715-paid-complex`): #458's full
wrapper and the R715 package's full wrapper from scratch, then the exact composition (two moment engines per side, six bootstrap
levels, all 47 strict outer inequalities, next-grid and parameter controls). The bit package regenerates the word from its frozen
hierarchy (legality of every rule and read checked), runs #370's independent all-column checker and mutants, a relaxed copy of that
checker on the kernel and mixed words, #443's C++ cohort legality and formal columns at five and eleven stages, mixing mutants, Gram,
eleven-stage template and hosting audits, and its own assembly. Two fresh-copy runs agree apart from timing fields (results, both
supplier RESULTs and the complex AUDIT byte-equal). The R715 word was also checked by an independent validator.

**Review points**
- **Carrier bound** (proof above): the 4-design identity for E7 and the frame-containment argument give ≥ 240 carriers; it is a
  scoped bound for this format, not used by the certificate.
- **Rekid legality**: each of the 11 re-expressed rules uses existing symbols whose frames lie inside the rule's frame, the
  hierarchy stays acyclic (the compiler's recursion requires it), every consumer frame contains the rule's frame, and content equals
  the F2 sum of its kids (checked by `hier_word.py` before compiling).

cross-family splitting derivation used there. This construction keeps every residual in one whole family.

## Two construction mechanisms

1. **Whole-residual pooling across replicas.** Allocate the eight replicas jointly rather than solve
   identical per-replica integer packing problems. Every helper stays on one physical array family,

respectively. Structural sources include Mathlib's block-diagonal multiplication and the project's

title: Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension
body:
**Format obstructions (no new κ): exact bounds on window width, copy cost and label dimension, checked on `gx.check1` programs and on #425's mutable-basis word.** This is a research package of statements, proofs and
exact checks. It claims no new κ. It fixes what three formats can and cannot do and shows where the remaining
freedom is.

| | statement | checked on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | a contribution that reaches a register by a drop-free path forces its frame to contain the source label, so lossless x_T → y_S needs orthogonal labels | every gate of the p = 3, p = 10 (#327) and p = 11 (#193) programs: 0 violations in 3.1 M gate checks |
| **B** | k_a + Σ_j rk C_j ≤ m; with corrector rank h − 1, m ≥ 1 + s(h − 1) | rank h − 1 on all families (replayed correctors for the complex programs and #425; in-cap neighbourhoods for the bit and E8 rows); **#425's word has m = 73 = 1 + 9·8, so the bound is attained** |
| **C** | the drops that carry a total to its readers cost at least rk(U(P) × U(Q)) | equality: 360 (p = 10), 440 (p = 11), 72 (#425 centres, 57 gathered sources each); for the E8 bit dual the package computes the bound 72, which equals the copy loss #370 reports (not replayed) |
| clique bound | Σ_K k_T ≤ r on a clique of drop-free pairs | ω = p (bit), 8, 8, 12, 12 (complex, p = 4..7); 20 ports pairwise lossless in the p = 10 program; ω = 8 on E8 |
| E8 labels | the h = 9 labelling of the E8 in-cap graph is unique; no k = 2 labelling in dimension ≤ 17 | exact SAT, with calibrations and a positive control |
| **P** | for fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ (one helper set, same slots, slot-carried pairs spanning) the stage windows are orthogonal, m ≥ s·h, under (P1)–(P2) | computed on the complex #327 and #193 programs only (399/400, 483/484). **Compressed windows circumvent it**: #425 (m = 73 < 81) and, for the bit word, #386 (m = 64; Theorem P is not claimed for ℚ forms). Not a general obstruction |
| **S** | a mutable-basis word with b_x modified sources and b_y read targets is simulated in the immutable-source / no-target-read format with R + b_x + b_y helpers | exact on #425's word: 904 = 680 + 112 + 112 |

**What this means for the swarm.** A–C and the clique bound bound m and the copy rank, the label dimension for a given
in-cap graph, and (through the five-stage ledger D ≤ N_data·k, read from upstream) D. They do **not** bound the
helper count R, nor the idle and stock costs, which is where #425, #433 and #442 gained. A further κ gain in these
formats has to come from R or the stock, or from a new port family whose corrector rank is below h − 1 with a cheap
decoder.

```sh
python -m pip install -r research/format-obstructions/requirements.txt    # python-sat 1.9.dev15, networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5
python3 -B research/format-obstructions/verify.py --output /tmp/format-obstructions-out   # about 90 s on 12 cores (15 CPU-minutes), no network
```

## What changed

One new self-contained package, `research/format-obstructions/`, plus its path-filtered workflow. No existing file
changes. Vendored byte for byte (sha256 in `SOURCE.json`): Jacob Sussman's `gx.py`, the p = 11 certificate of #193, the
p = 10 program of #327, #425's `FULL-WORD.json.gz` (regenerated with its own scripts; the sha equals its
`EXPECTED.json`), the cost model of #346 (from #310) and the p = 10 bit histogram of #325. The one local input is the
p = 3 toy program.

## What `verify.py` checks

It verifies the pins, then runs 91 tasks in a process pool and compares every number with `expected.json`:
- `gx.check1` with the exact scalar identity on the three programs, the taint replay of Theorem A at every gate, the
  corrector ranks of Theorem B and the copy bounds of Theorem C;
- the p = 3 toy: split scatter, cst 18 → 16, exhaustive optimum over all cut chains;
- Theorem P (rank of the cross-Gram constraints), the forced-copy count (10 per overlap, exact over all odd a, b) and
  the contamination scan (1,160 candidate directions);
- #425's word: frame and taint replay, exact scalar replay over ℚ, the Theorem S conversion and its replay;
- the pinned pricer on the p = 10 bit histogram (pinned root reproduced; context only);
- the E8 SAT checks: uniqueness at h = 9, k = 2 at r = 16 (255 patterns) and r = 17 (256), all UNSAT.

Negative controls: shifted labels and a corrupted port; a toy cut outside the radical; the immutable/no-target-read
detector flags 1,640 source modifications and 112 target reads on #425's word and 0 on the converted word; omitted K
and omitted compensation rejected; k = 1 at r = 8 UNSAT and r = 9 SAT, h = 8 UNSAT, the k = 2 encoder at r = 18 accepts
the direct sum.

## Verification

- **Replays:** two fresh-copy runs in other working directories (macOS, Python 3.12.14, python-sat 1.9.dev15,
  networkx 3.7, mpmath 1.3.0, numpy 2.3.5) pass every check; CI has not been run yet.
- **Independent audit:** Independent read-only audit (separate Claude agent): two blockers found and fixed; re-verified.

## Status, honestly

- **κ:** no new κ.
- **Scope:** Theorems A–C and the clique bound are proved for the frame model of PROOF.md §1, which contains the rules E0–E3
  of `gx.check1` and #425's common-label rule; the correspondence is by reading, with no mechanical proof and no Lean.
- **Layout hypotheses:** (B1)–(B2) of Theorem B and (P1)–(P2) of Theorem P were read against Sussman's
  `Work/Bridge/Net.lean`, `Work/BridgeGeom/Stage.lean` and `Work/BridgeGeom/Net.lean` (f010392c); they are consistent
  with the statements there, but this was read, not formally verified. Two points are open: whether the backward stages
  1 and 3 count as "the same program", and whether the stage-j target frames lie in ι_j(q_S)^⊥. Theorem P holds for
  fixed-role B₂ windows over F₂ only; #425's nine-stage windows (m = 73) are outside it.
- **Bit side:** no bit word is replayed. Theorem P (stated for F₂ windows) and the overlap measurements were computed on
  complex programs, and nothing is claimed about Theorem P for ℚ forms such as #386's; the pricing context uses the
  p = 10 bit histogram (the file copied from the `math.json` that #325's verification writes) and is a pricer-model
  output.
- **Theorem S:** a bound on helper count, not on price (the simulation prices 13 % below #425's word under the coarse
  formula). Replayed by the package's detector on #425's word, not by `gx.check1`.
- **E8 labels:** the SAT results are for the full E8 in-cap graph only.

## Attribution

- **Jacob Sussman:** gcert/1, `gx.check1`, the frame lemma, the five-stage layout and the E8 complex unit.
- **jacklightChen (Zhihao Chen):** #425's word and its conjugation semantics; #386.
- **Dylan Crow (utcorvusvolat-dotcom):** #370 (E8 bit word, root coordinates) and the #310 cost model.
- **Louis Harrison:** #346 (the vendored pricer).
- **Avi Eisenberg (ikeboy):** #193. **icekylinx:** #144, #184 and #433. **chafreaky:** #200, #233, #256.
- **eumemic:** #168. **DaysSky:** #162, #352 and #442. **hcg890** and **SovereignSteak:** #234 and the five-stage ledger.

The statements, proofs, checks and packaging were prepared by DreamingOfClouds with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via
Claude Code. Every upstream notice is retained; see `NOTICE`.

The package applies to `main` at `3b6b66891c0ac888521cf591fe306c6286601d4f` (which integrates #186 on top of my #181 and eumemic's #168) and is mergeable there; its construction inputs are PR168 v4 at `4a3c769e5c5430e7114c4d3e099ff34664677f17`, and the twelve PR168 v4 files it executes or pins are vendored byte-identically with digests in `references/pr168-v4`, so no file outside the package changes. Two changes above PR168 v4. **Complex:** a new per-cube local channel circuit found by 240 random restarts over PR144's $3^{13}$ circuit options and two coordinate-descent rounds, scored by the numerical physical root: $A[0,0]$, $A[0,1]$ and $A[1,1]$ are assembled from the two face diagonals, $A[1,0]$ from direction-2 edges, $A[2,\cdot]$ from direction-1 edges; $G[0,1,\cdot]$ and $G[0,2,1]$ use edge differences and $G[0,2,0]$, $G[1,2,0]$, $G[1,2,1]$ use fixed-coordinate differences. The circuit has 33 additions per cube instead of 27, but the carrier closure admits 12,189 arcs instead of 10,704, so the virtual auxiliary stock falls from 13,372 to 12,877 roles. All modules, fused outputs and schedules of PR168 are retained; the carrier matching, gauge selection, endpoint frame descent, 2,310 compensated handoffs and 44 terminal-output deletions are regenerated for the new graph. **Bit (new, beyond my #189/#196):** a per-cube bit local circuit found by 100 random restarts and three coordinate-descent rounds over the bit circuit options, each candidate priced through the full physical pipeline: $A[0,0]$, $A[0,1]$, $A[2,0]$ and $A[2,1]$ from the two face diagonals, $A[1,\cdot]$ from direction-0 edges, $G[0,1,0]$ from fixed-coordinate differences (edges elsewhere). The bit virtual stock falls from 19,788 to 18,908 roles (modules, L1 association, partner mixing and output merge unchanged). For this graph a fresh carrier matching and gauge selection are regenerated by the retained generator rules, a complete physical layer (7,282 descended operation frames, 1,760 compensated handoffs) is built by our own producer, and 34 face0 terminal sinks are deleted by James Chang's PR166 substitution. Both suppliers and the paid balanced composition are independently certified. Under the retained interfaces, the bound is

$$
T(n)=O\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{166261725903847}{25\cdot10^{16}}
=0.000665046903615388.
$$

Same headline as my #196 (complex-bound); this PR adds the stronger bit supplier. The refined complex profile has 10,523 physical auxiliary roles, 13,163 persistent roles, rank mass 867,438, deficit 1,320 and largest child 20; its saving is $665489485337/10^{15}=0.000665489485337$. The new bit profile has 17,114 physical roles, 20,634 persistent roles, rank mass 1,483,712, deficit 1,936 and largest child 60; its coarse saving is $677773948354561/10^{18}=0.000677773948355$ (PR189: $0.000668298937776$; PR168 v4: $6600253/10^{10}$), and the established atom wrapper gives ordinary saving approximately **0.000677340914792**, 1.42% above the PR189 bit supplier that #194 composes with. Composed with the source-assisted complex word of #193/#194 (saving 7.009e-4) it would give about 6.769e-4, which I am preparing as a separate stacked composition with full credit.

The configurable circuit is icekylinx's (PR144); the complex part only selects a different configuration. Carrier arcs come from our own legal-edge Hopcroft–Karp matching on coordinate-padded frames, extended by DaysSky's PR162 rule, and are replayed by the retained `compile_closure` with its acyclicity and span checks. The new bit graph is admitted through the retained package checker (exact rational frames, mod-2 decoder, geometry, chains, partner chronology, F2 replay, ledger and five mutation controls). The physical bit layer follows PR131's descent rule (each frame between the join of its incoming frames and the meet of its outgoing frames) on exact rational subspaces, repaired to nondegenerate bases, with handoffs read at the recipient's first use; the 34 sinks are the face0 roots whose rank-21 caps contain every write, with the complete modified target chronology, all 17,114 dirty columns over F2 and over the integers, and exact prime witnesses for all 24,401 used frames. title: Conditional κ = 1.128983115440183e-3: an E8 bit word with 740 helpers under #433's complex supplier
body:
#433 (icekylinx) is bit-bound: its complex supplier has b = 1183986549206329/10¹⁸, and its R758 bit word gives c ≈ 1.122123e-3. This PR replaces the bit word with an E8 bit word with **R = 740 helpers**, in #386's compressed nine-stage layout. Pricing uses #433's own bit engine, finite invoice and six-level tail.

**κ = 1128983115440183/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.128983115440183e-3**, bit-bound. That is **+0.7243 % over #433** (560432476129139/(5·10¹⁷)). It is also above #435 (1.128832830332521e-3, #417's kernel on #433's R758 word) and #434, which were posted while this was being prepared. The kernel of #417/#435 and this word's reuse are different mechanisms; stacking them is not attempted here.

| layout | bit c of this word | best published in that layout | gain |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| compressed nine-stage (#386; used by #425, #431, #433) | 282564789736676592463/(2.5·10²³) ≈ 1.130259e-3 | #433 (R758) | +0.725 % |
| B₄ unsplit (#381) | 1064525457834209/10¹⁸ ≈ 1.064525e-3 | #417 | +1.960 % |

One self-contained package, `research/e8-bit-elimination-reuse/`, with its own workflow, plus one `.gitattributes` line. No existing file changes.

### Mechanism

1. **#370's producer with new parameters** (67 of 520 entries changed) gives R = 863.
2. **Elimination reuse of dead helper slots** gives R 863 → 740.
   - A dead helper still holds a leftover x-content, an F₂ sum of source lines.
   - Before a later helper is born at frame F, take an F₂ relation among the leftovers of dead slots inside F. One gate at the join of their frames empties one slot, and the new helper takes it over.
   - The 9 retained totals also take dead slots; their leftover lines are read at the full frame.
   - 114 slots are reused by helpers and 9 by totals.
3. **Single-gate frame retiming**, #389's idea: 37 gate moves.

**Overlap.**
- #426 (ai-nanachi) published the same slot-reuse mechanism first: 55 "clean resets" on #376's R822 word, giving R767. We developed this pass independently. On a different base word it finds 114 reuses plus the 9 totals.
- #433's nine-sum source-basis change frees no register here, because the totals already sit on dead slots.

### Checks

`bash research/e8-bit-elimination-reuse/verify.sh [--quick] DIR`: about 40 s quick, 67 s full.

- **Provenance.** Manifest; 52 vendored files pinned by git blob id. Every cited complex b and κ must equal that PR's own receipt.
- **Rebuild.** The word is rebuilt from pinned inputs and must equal the shipped word. #370's producer regenerates #370's word as a control.
- **#370's independent checker:** exact F₂ on all 980 columns with dirty helpers, and Gram determinants > 0 on every frame (only prime 2). 6 word-level and 6 reuse-specific mutants are rejected.
- **Official checkers.** PR #266's legality at NCOPY = 9; NCOPY = 8 is rejected. Five-stage and B₄ formal columns, with 18 omitted-bridge controls rejected.
- **#386 layout.** Geometry, source-bound template, audit and price.
- **#433's engine, invoice and tail.** These reproduce #433's own c and κ exactly, and #386's, #425's and #431's κ. The tail uses 47 strict inequalities; the next grid point, zero η, zero β and unit β are rejected.
- **B₄.** #381's geometry, banks (T = 9), finite bill and price.
- **Local build.** The C++ checkers were built against an overflow-checked 128-bit stand-in for `boost::multiprecision::cpp_int`, because the preparing machine has no Boost. In CI, the package workflow built them with libboost-dev and passed on Python 3.12 and 3.14.
- **Repository CI.** This branch includes rohanarun's #318 three-file joint-dual pin repair (byte-identical to a45747d), as #417 and #439 do, so the repository joint check passes.

### Retained assumptions

- Everything #370 admits: 9 retained totals at h = 8, PR234's banks for a non-paired-cube family, and the all-size bit compiler, prime, tape, precision and analytic interfaces.
- #386's compressed-layout arguments, including two-level halving (max child 42/64).
- #433's complex supplier is cited, not rebuilt. Its proof rests on #425's written scalar-interface extension.
- This is a conditional finite construction, not a Lean proof.

### Credits

utcorvusvolat-dotcom / Dylan Crow (#370: format, producer, checkers); applecrusher (#376); ai-nanachi (#389 retiming; #426 clean-reset reuse, published first); icekylinx (#433 complex supplier, bit engine, invoice and tail); DaysSky (#381, #375, #363); Zhihao Chen / jacklightChen (#386, #425); Chafik Boukhalfa / chafreaky (#417); Rohan Arun (#392, #431); Jacob Sussman (E8, bridged word); the PR #266 and PR #315 (DreamingOfClouds) lineage. Vendored files are byte-identical and listed in `NOTICE.md` and `SOURCE-pr*.json`.

title: Split centres and source-basis reuse for conditional κ = 0.001120864952258278
body:
This combines a new split-centre complex construction with source-centre reuse on the bit side, in one commit based on main at `12a4934d15006e8c10f9b2264f13f8f341be802b`.

Under the retained compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{560432476129139}{500000000000000000}
=0.001120864952258278.
$$

The combined saving is approximately **6.9522% above [#425](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/425)**. The bit supplier binds the new assembly.

## Construction

On the complex side, cancel the coordinate-source contributions that appear with opposite signs in the centre and side decoders before lifting them to address operators. The 112 code-line targets then use eight rank-eight centres; the eight coordinate targets use rank-one identity copies. Their total copied rank remains 72. Removing 112 coordinate-source helpers and eight dedicated full-centre helpers reduces R from 680 to 560. The dirty response is recomputed from the new word, and both orientations include literal source/helper cleanup and exact heterogeneous-centre phases.

On the bit side, start from #426's R767 word. Form its nine retained sums with an invertible basis change on the source rows, copy them sequentially, and apply the literal inverse before continuing. This removes nine helpers. Compose the resulting R758 word with the compressed dimension-64 geometry from #386, replaying the actual reflected copy chronology and all new bank owners. The changed prefix needs 223 bits and is charged at 256 bits; the old 192-bit allowance is not reused.

| Selected supplier | Complex | Bit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ambient dimension | 73 | 64 |
| Auxiliary rows | 560 | 758 |
| Live recursion stock | 12,720 | 14,502 |

Three separately scoped exact negative proofs document limits of frozen-center bases, arbitrary rank-eight completions, and fixed first-frame/full-residual bank budgets; none asserts a global impossibility for changed architectures.

For context: jacklightChen's #425 (≈1.048005508e-3) and its follow-up #431 use a Hamming-packet complex network under their own lemma, in place of gx's source-immutability and target-read rules. They are not comparable under these checkers.

The complex side binds: b = 255198274817418511443/2.5·10²³ ≈ 1.020793e-3. The bit side is #404's pinned c ≈ 1.021539e-3 > b.

### Construction (`code/compose426.py`)
1. **Input: #426's R779 gauged word**, pinned byte-for-byte (blob 0daa4323), with 202 gauges after the 556/577 helper inlining.
   - Control: our own emitter and price, at #426's 8 replicas and bank patterns, reproduce #426's complex coefficient 254951444354246755323/2.5·10²³ and its profile exactly.
   - Re-implementing the two substitutions directly on #398's signed R781 word (our #424 base) is frame-infeasible, so we start from #426's word.

3. **Fourteen fixed-scalar gate-frame retimings: 12 single gates and 2 five-gate blocks.**
